chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from 'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had a slave mother. When death approached him, a man from our companions went and bought her mother, stipulating upon her: 'If I buy you and free you, and when your son so-and-so dies and you inherit him, you give me half of what you inherit, on condition that you give me the pledge of God and the pledge of His Messenger that you will fulfill this for me.' The man bought her and freed her on that condition. Then her son died, and she inherited him, and there was no other heir for him. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'He has done well to her and will be rewarded for it. Indeed, this is a jurist, and Muslims are bound by their conditions, and it is upon her to fulfill for him what she pledged to God and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on conditional manumission and inheritance agreements in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia legal principle of *al-muslimuna 'inda shurutihim* (Muslims are bound by their stipulations) within the specific context of *kitabah* or conditional manumission. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the agreement, highlighting that the mother’s fulfillment of the oath to Allah and the Prophet serves as the binding mechanism for the transfer of inheritance rights, thereby linking contractual fidelity to religious devotion.
